newsitem.title: USA: Black coalition to continue boycott against Texaco.
newsitem.headline: Black coalition to continue boycott against Texaco.

text.p: A black coalition said Tuesday that it would continue to boycott Texaco Inc until it produced a plan with goals and timetables to hire and promote more blacks and other minorities.

Texaco officials Tuesday updated the Rainbow Coalition and other black and minority groups on its effort to lay out a specific plan for hiring more blacks and other minorities, changing the make-up of its board, using more minority vendors and investing in minority owned businesses.

Black leaders said they were very disappointed with the progress to date, and would resume picketing Texaco service stations. The picketing had been called off two weeks ago when Texaco reached a landmark $176 million settlement of a race bias suit.
"It was disappointing," said Kweisi Mfume, head of the National Association for the Advancement of Colored People.
"I expect by December 13, if not before, we will have a draft of a proposal that will either be acceptable or non-acceptable," Mfume said.
"I would consider it a breach of commitment (by Texaco Chairman Peter Bijur) if it's not acceptable," he told Reuters.
Mfume said so far Texaco had done very little preparation for its minority plan.

Mfume said if Texaco failed to come up with a good plan by the middle of December, his group would go ahead with preparations to encourage pension funds, state and local government funds and colleges and universities to divest their holdings of Texaco stock.
